- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days to avoid overreaction.
- In absence of strong sentiment, model often underestimates mean-reversion trend; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% if recent 5-day average is below 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and model forecasts are rising, reduce forecast by 2–4% to reflect bearish sentiment bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period price surge; add 1–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment turns positive mid-horizon.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (≤0.2) and model consistently overestimates, apply a 3–5% downward bias to all forecasts in that sentiment regime.
